issue: The in-plot annotation '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)' is ambiguous: the figure plots two GQA curves (GQA FP8 ~0.33 MB/tok and GQA FP16 ~0.66 MB/tok), and 3.1 GB corresponds only to the GQA FP8 curve (9,500 x 0.33 MB = 3.1 GB; GQA FP16 would be 6.2 GB). evidence: Legend lists 'GQA FP8 (~0.33 MB/tok)' and 'GQA FP16 (~0.66 MB/tok)' as separate series; the annotation names only 'GQA'. The companion annotation '9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' is unambiguous because only one full-MHA FP16 curve exists.
acceptance_test: Relabel to '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA FP8)' and confirm the leader line terminates on the GQA FP8 marker.

issue: The annotation '8x saving (Ch. 7)' has no visible anchor or leader line, so the reader cannot determine which pair of curves it compares (full-MHA FP16 vs GQA FP8, or full-MHA FP16 vs GQA FP16, which is only 4x).
evidence: The other two in-plot annotations ('9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)', '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)') carry leader lines to their markers; '8x saving (Ch. 7)' is free-floating text in the upper-right of the plot area.

figure: Figure 7.6 — Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning
issue: The 2×H100 (160 GB) reference line crosses the inference bar near its top, and the bar's hatching can obscure the dashed line at print size. The inference bar is only ~5 GB above the line, so the visual relationship is easy to misread.
evidence: The inference bar is ~165 GB; the 2×H100 line is at 160 GB. The line is dashed gray and the bar is hatched blue. The caption says inference is ~165 GB.

figure: Figure 7.6 — Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning
issue: Ambiguous exclusion note: 'Adapter rank, activation, and offload are NOT included (Table 7-2)' can be read as 'adapter memory is not included,' directly contradicting the bar label 'QLoRA (weights+adapters)' and the composition note '4-bit (NF4) base + LoRA adapters + a small optimizer.' A hasty reader may conclude the ~60 GB bar excludes adapters entirely, or conversely may not understand what 'adapter rank' means as an excluded item.
evidence: Bar label reads 'QLoRA (weights+adapters)'; composition note reads 'QLoRA: 4-bit (NF4) base + LoRA adapters + a small optimizer'; exclusion note reads 'Adapter rank, activation, and offload are NOT included (Table 7-2).' The term 'Adapter rank' in an exclusion list alongside 'activation' and 'offload' (both clearly memory categories) invites the reading that adapter memory itself is excluded.
acceptance_test: Rephrase the exclusion to remove ambiguity, e.g., 'Specific adapter-rank value, activation memory, and offload/checkpointing are NOT included (Table 7-2)' or split into 'Adapter memory for a specific rank value, activation, and offload are NOT included.' Confirm the rephrased note is consistent with the bar label and composition note.

issue: The note enumerating the full-fine-tune memory components does not sum to the plotted bar value of ~1,120 GB. As rendered it reads 'Full-tune: FP16 weights + FP16 grads + Adam m/v (2 x 16 B/param).' The listed components either give 2+2+32 = 36 B/param (2,520 GB) or, if the parenthetical is '2 x 4 B/param', 2+2+8 = 12 B/param (840 GB). Neither equals the plotted 1,120 GB.
evidence: 1,120 GB / 70e9 params = 16 B/param exactly. The only standard mixed-precision Adam configuration that yields 16 B/param is FP16 weights (2) + FP16 grads (2) + FP32 master weights (4) + FP32 Adam m (4) + FP32 Adam v (4) = 16 B/param -> 1,120 GB. The FP32 master-weight copy is not visible in the note as rendered, so the figure's own derivation does not close.
acceptance_test: Verify the source string for the note. If the FP32 master copy is absent, add it and state the total explicitly ('16 B/param -> 1,120 GB'); if the parenthetical reads '2 x 16 B/param', correct it to '2 x 4 B/param'. Acceptance: the note's components sum to the plotted bar value, and the sum is shown.

issue: The first note appears to have an unbalanced parenthesis: 'Each bar is a conditional floor (weights + the listed states, not a full deployment config.' with no closing parenthesis before the period.
evidence: Visible on the rendered page (printed p. 124, first note line). The same note block otherwise uses balanced parentheses ('(2 x 16 B/param)', '(Table 7-2)').
acceptance_test: Check the source string and close the parenthesis (or restructure the sentence). Re-render and confirm punctuation balance across all five note lines.

issue: The 'Inference (weights+KV)' bar (~165 GB) visibly crosses the '2xH100 (160 GB)' reference line, but the figure annotates only the QLoRA bar ('QLoRA fits a single H100') and the full-fine-tune bar ('Full fine-tune exceeds an 8xH100 host: needs multi-node or offload'). acceptance_test: Add an annotation on the inference bar stating the implication (e.g. 'Inference exceeds 2xH100 (160 GB) at 9.5K context') so all three bars carry the same interpretive treatment.

issue: The KV term in the inference bar is not attributed to an attention geometry. The bar's ~165 GB = 140 GB FP16 weights + ~24.9 GB KV, and 24.9 GB is the full-MHA FP16 bound at 9.5K (per FIG 7.5). A reader who has just absorbed FIG 7.1 and FIG 7.5 may assume the canonical model uses GQA and compute 140 + 6.2 = 146 GB, contradicting the bar.
evidence: FIG 7.5 annotation '9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' (full-MHA) vs '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)' (GQA FP8); FIG 7.6's caption says only 'weights + KV' with no geometry qualifier.
acceptance_test: State the geometry in the figure or caption, e.g. 'Inference (weights + full-MHA FP16 KV at 9.5K)', and cross-reference FIG 7.5 so the 24.9 GB term is traceable.

issue: The bar label says '~64 GB runtime' while the caption says '~64 GB runtime/NCCL'; the figure omits NCCL, which is part of the budget.
acceptance_test: Change the label to 'runtime/NCCL' or add a footnote; verify the figure and caption use the same term.

figure: FIGURE 7.7 — Concurrency budget — one 8×H100 host (640 GB pool)
issue: The displayed substitution line under the figure reads "≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests". The operator between the two quantities is a plus sign, but the arithmetic requires division (436 ÷ 24.9 = 17.51). As printed, the equation is false: 436 + 24.9 = 460.9, not 17.5. It also contradicts the line immediately above it, which correctly states "in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request".
evidence: Rendered page 145, display block between the bar and the caption: line 1 "in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request"; line 2 "≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests". Caption confirms the intended operation: "at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C = 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18…)". 436 ÷ 24.9 = 17.51 ✓; 436 + 24.9 = 460.9 ✗. The same figure's caption also uses the correct division for the FP8 case (436 ÷ 12.45 ≈ 35).
acceptance_test: Open the source for the FIGURE 7.7 display and confirm the operator glyph is '÷' (or ' / '), not '+'. If the source is correct, re-render at 300 dpi and confirm the glyph is a division sign on the page; if the source is wrong, change '+' to '÷' and re-check that the display still reads "≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests". Also confirm no downstream text quotes the '+' form.

issue: The caption sentence is grammatically broken and logically ambiguous: "and that KV budget is the per-request KV price sets concurrency". The intended relation (budget ÷ per-request price = concurrency) is not stated; as written the sentence has no main verb and could be read as claiming the budget *is* the price.
evidence: Rendered page 145, caption line 2–3: "…host's 640 GB pool, and that KV budget is the per-request KV price sets concurrency — at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C = 17.5 concurrent…". The figure's own display (line 1) states the correct relation, so the caption is the only place the relation is stated in words.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as: "…and that KV budget, divided by the per-request KV price, sets concurrency — at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C = 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18…)". Confirm the rewritten sentence names both operands and the operation.

issue: The "~64 GB runtime" segment and the "~436 GB KV budget" segment are drawn with the same green fill and the same white label treatment; only the weights segment is distinguished by a blue diagonal hatch. In grayscale the three-way decomposition of the 640 GB pool reduces to one green block plus one hatched block, and the runtime/KV boundary is carried only by a hairline and by the text inside a very narrow box. The runtime label is also set noticeably smaller than the weights label and is squeezed into a ~0.2 in box, wrapping onto two lines.
evidence: Rendered page 145: blue hatched "140 GB weights" (label ~9 pt) vs green "~64 GB runtime" (label ~7.5 pt, two lines, box ~30 px wide at 150 dpi) vs green "~436 GB KV budget". No legend or pattern key is present on the page.
acceptance_test: Give the runtime segment a distinct fill (e.g. a different hatch or a lighter tint) so the three components are separable in grayscale, and set the runtime label at the same size as the other two segment labels (or move it above the bar with a leader line). Confirm by rendering the page to grayscale and checking that all three segments remain distinguishable without reading the labels.

issue: "640 GB pool" is set as a free-floating label at the far right of the title line, horizontally aligned with the right end of the bar, where it can be misread as a label for the rightmost (KV) band rather than for the whole pool. The figure also never states that bar width is proportional to GB, so a reader cannot tell whether the three segments are drawn to scale (140 : 64 : 436).

acceptance_test: Move "640 GB pool" immediately after the title text (or into the title itself: "Concurrency budget — one 8×H100 host, 640 GB pool"), and add a one-line note such as "bar width ∝ GB" to the figure or caption. Confirm the drawn segment widths are proportional to 140 : 64 : 436 within a few percent.

issue: The caption makes a specific, load-bearing claim about a graphic feature — "the faint vertical rules inside the KV band are those 24.9 GB request slots" — but the rules are drawn at very low contrast. At print size (and in the 150 dpi render) they are barely perceptible, so the reader cannot count the slots or see the 17.5-slot fractional remainder that the caption's "floor 17, not 18" argument depends on.

issue: Gratuitous visual-encoding inconsistency for the same three components of the same 640 GB 8×H100 pool across two adjacent Ch 7 figures. Weights are consistent (blue diagonal hatch) in both, but the KV component is a GREEN band with vertical slot lines in 7.7 yet an ORANGE dotted band in 7.8, and the runtime component is a SOLID dark-gray box in 7.7 yet a LIGHT-gray cross-hatched box in 7.8. issue: The caption says 'only ~1–2 at 128K', but the figure's own KV 335 GB and the fixed 436 GB KV budget imply 436/335 ≈ 1.30, i.e., one full request, not two.

figure: FIGURE 7.8 — Memory Tetris (scale note vs. drawing)
issue: The figure's own note says "Bar heights are not to scale (GB)", yet the drawing is (or appears to be) to scale: the light horizontal rules are spaced at 80 GB intervals across the 640 GB pool, and the three bar tops land at roughly 36% / 45% / 84% of the 640 GB dashed line, i.e. 229 / 288 / 539 GB. One of the two statements is false. If the note is true, then the "640 GB = 8× 80 GB ranks" dashed line and the "light rules = 80 GB rank boundaries" are meaningless decoration and the reader will misread the 128K bar as nearly filling the host. If the note is false, the note is a factual error in the figure.
evidence: Rendered page 146: note under the bars reads "The baseline (weights + runtime) is fixed; only the KV cache grows with context. Bar heights are not to scale (GB)." Against that: the red dashed 640 GB line sits above all three bars; the light rules are evenly spaced at ~1/8 of the plot height (consistent with 80 GB × 8); bar tops are at ≈229/288/539 GB, which are exactly the values printed under the bars ("= 229 GB used", "= 288 GB used", "= 539 GB used").
acceptance_test: Decide which is intended and make them agree: (a) if to scale, delete "Bar heights are not to scale (GB)" and replace with "Bar heights are to scale (GB); light rules are 80 GB capacity gridlines"; (b) if not to scale, remove the 640 GB dashed line and the 80 GB rules and add the fill fractions numerically ("229/640 = 36%", "288/640 = 45%", "539/640 = 84%"). Verify by measuring the rendered bar tops against the 640 GB line.

evidence: Visual: bars stack runtime at bottom, weights above, KV on top; legend lists KV first, weights second, runtime third.
